purpose: The personal half of the publishability contract for this fictional candidate. An id names what a marker is, never what it matches: the report counts every declared marker, so the ids are printed on every run, and an id spelling the employer would walk past the rule that a finding never carries its matched text. Everything here names one person, which is why it lives in the layer and never in the public tree: printed in the open, the list would reveal exactly what it hides. tools/publishability/README.md owns the shape, the public markers and the refusal codes.

markers.why: The candidate's surname, in every script the materials use.
The account name that appears in paths and remotes.
The local part of the address, which survives a changed domain.
An employer from the candidate's history.
An employer from the candidate's history.
A company the candidate applied to.
The country of residence, which the scoring constraints depend on.
The profile file name, which code and tests would otherwise reach by path.

allow.why: The ISO-3166 table is reference data of the engine, not a fact about the candidate.
A country inside a captured vacancy page is somebody else's text.
